detail.longDescription: Reading List – 2026-10-30 I’m thinking about what it takes to put agents to work responsibly. Fewer tokens per task don’t settle the question of production cost, and an agent’s authority needs to be clear before it acts. Separately, remembering Patrick Stewart brings me back to Picard’s mix of listening and decisive leadership. Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now Open Weight Token efficiency matters alongside benchmark scores when coding agents make many model calls. Mistral reports that Large 4 scored 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, roughly matching GLM-5.3 while using 47% fewer tokens per task. What catches my attention is the possibility of reducing agent costs without giving up measured performance. For a production workflow, I'd compare total costs and code quality on representative repository tasks, not token counts alone. Agent identity startup Mintive lands Cowboy Ventures, Coatue, angels Jeff Dean, Andrej Karpathy An agent’s permissions may need to differ from those of the employee it serves. Mintive says its platform handles agent identities and authorization, with an MCP gateway controlling access to cloud services and actions. What catches my attention is the operational tradeoff: hiding permissioning complexity may speed deployment, but teams still need to understand what authority an agent has when it acts across services. Gemini in-chat document and PDF creation and editing Gemini now lets you revise generated files inside the chat by highlighting content and asking for a change. Google gives the example of selecting a table and asking Gemini to turn it into a graph. What catches my attention is the shorter loop between reviewing a draft and directing a revision. For now, PDF editing works on mobile, but other formats require the web version. Gemini’s in-chat editing lets users correct generated files without starting over, including highlighting a section for Gemini to revise text or visuals. What catches my attention is the mix of manual corrections and targeted AI edits: users can retain the parts that work. Device support is a practical constraint, though: PDF editing works on mobile and web, while Docs, Sheets, presentations, Markdown, TXT, and code are web-only. You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now · Google Gemini can now create and edit PDFs, documents, and more right inside your chat OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT Thrive Holdings plans to build a smart home security business around ADT, but hasn't said what AI products it will release. OpenAI supplies models, technology, and forward-deployed engineers to Thrive's companies. What catches my attention is the gap between acquiring an established security business and explaining how AI will change its products. For engineers evaluating those products, the acquisition alone says little about their behavior or reliability. Patrick Stewart’s death and career tributes The report says Patrick Stewart will appear posthumously as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday, scheduled for December. What catches my attention is that the role sits alongside his long association with Captain Jean-Luc Picard, whom he first played in Star Trek: The Next Generation. The article also points to a wider stage and screen career, though it offers few details beyond those two franchises. Patrick Stewart’s portrayal of Jean-Luc Picard stretched from The Next Generation’s 1987 debut to Star Trek: Nemesis in 2002. His death at 86 closes a career that began in theater and included Professor Xavier in the X-Men films. I’m struck by how long Stewart returned to Picard: four films followed the series, giving audiences more years with the character beyond its original television run. The tributes to Patrick Stewart reach beyond Captain Picard to a career on stage and screen. Hugh Jackman remembers Stewart as a friend and someone he learned from, while William Shatner recalls the intelligence and humanity he brought to his work. What catches my attention is how those personal recollections sit alongside Marvel’s tribute to his portrayal of Charles Xavier. Together, they show the breadth of the roles and relationships people are mourning. Patrick Stewart’s career stretched well beyond the science-fiction roles that made him an icon. I’m struck by the range represented in his Emmy and Golden Globe nominations, from Moby Dick and Hamlet to Extras and Blunt Talk. Captain Jean-Luc Picard and Professor Charles Xavier may be his most familiar roles, but they’re only part of the work he leaves behind. Patrick Stewart’s Picard brought a diplomat’s composure to the Enterprise, a contrast with James T. Kirk’s swashbuckling style. I’m struck by how The Next Generation tested that composure: the Borg assimilated Picard, and he struggled to recover afterward. That story gave a commanding character room for vulnerability, making the cost of what happened to him part of his character. Stewart has died at 86. Patrick Stewart’s portrayal of Captain Picard was a formative influence on my management style. Picard was collaborative and open to feedback, yet decisive when it mattered. When I lived in London, I saw Stewart perform in several plays, and I’ll always remember his Prospero in The Tempest. Picard remains a model for listening without giving up the responsibility to decide. Patrick Stewart’s roles offer more to revisit than Captain Picard and Professor X. In Green Room, he plays Darcy Banker, a bar owner and the soft-spoken, violent leader of a white supremacist crowd. I’m struck by the contrast with his appearance as a heightened version of himself in Extras. Either offers a different starting point from his best-known franchises. What catches my attention is the remaining boundary around dictation: the article says Apple requires third-party keyboards to briefly open their own app before returning to yours. Pepper suggests events from email for you to accept, and asks before emailing people or sending invitations. Chris and I are really excited to hear what you think about our broader take on AI productivity: calendars, group chat, notes, tasks, and an agent always there to help. Its sidebar also shows which reporting agents are working, blocked, or done, making it easier to find work that needs attention.
